extracted.intended_audience: litigants and appellate counsel handling MSPB/EEO appeals to the Federal Circuit and district courts
extracted.subtask_description: Determining the correct forum and jurisdictional consequences when Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) appeals overlap with discrimination/EEO claims, and when transfer under 28 U.S.C. §1631 is appropriate. Focuses on whether the Federal Circuit or a federal district court has jurisdiction and on the permissibility of bifurcated review.

rubrics_metrics.name: District court jurisdiction for discrimination claims (5 U.S.C. § 7703(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal district courts, not this court, have jurisdiction over '[c]ases of discrimination subject to the provisions of [5 U.S.C. §] 7702,' 5 U.S.C. § 7703(b)(2)—i.e., where an employee has made a non-frivolous allegation regarding an action appealable to the Board and that the action was based, at least in part, on covered discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Perry v. Merit Sys. Prot. Bd., 582 U.S. 420, 437 (2017). Apply this standard when an EEO complaint alleges discriminatory personnel actions (e.g., alleged termination) and the discrimination allegation is non-frivolous; such matters belong in district court rather than the Federal Circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No bifurcated review — cannot split discrimination and non-discrimination claims between forums
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner cannot pursue non‑discrimination (civil‑service) issues in the Federal Circuit while challenging discrimination issues in district court; Congress did not direct or contemplate bifurcated review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Williams v. Dep’t of Army, 715 F.2d 1485, 1490 (Fed. Cir. 1983) (en banc) and related authority (e.g., Punch v. NASA). If claims are overlapping or related, litigants must not attempt to split forums for separate parts of the dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment must be actual; mere statement of intent to abandon is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: A corrected statement that purports to 'abandon' discrimination claims is not effective if the petitioner instead seeks to pursue those discrimination claims in a pending district court case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: courts will look to actual posture of the claims and whether the petitioner is seeking overlapping relief in multiple fora; strategic or partial abandonment that leaves parallel proceedings undermines the court's jurisdiction and is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap of relief triggers lack of jurisdiction in the court where overlap exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petitioner is seeking overlapping relief from both the Federal Circuit and a district court (e.g., challenging the same personnel action in different fora), the Federal Circuit lacks jurisdiction over the petition for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should assess whether relief sought in the petition overlaps with relief pending in district court; overlapping requests for relief weigh against Federal Circuit jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer to correct forum under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 when lacking jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: When this court lacks jurisdiction, transfer of the matter to the appropriate federal district court pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1631 is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the order: transfer to the United States District Court for the District of Columbia was appropriate because the petitioner was employed there and his discrimination claims were pending in that district. Use § 1631 to cure lack of jurisdiction by moving the filings to the proper court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence and consequences of EEO/agency/MSPB/district court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee may file an EEO complaint with an agency and seek administrative resolution; the agency's finding may be appealed to the MSPB, which can dismiss for lack of jurisdiction. Subsequent appeals must be brought in the proper forum depending on whether discrimination claims are implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the procedural posture: EEO complaint → agency decision → MSPB appeal (possible dismissal for lack of jurisdiction) → appeals to Federal Circuit only appropriate when jurisdictional prerequisites are met; otherwise district court review is required for discrimination claims.
